cover.title: Jesus’ Ministry
cover.subtitle: From Birth to Ascension: Miracles, Prophecies and Your Notes

overview:
Jesus’ Ministry: From Birth to Ascension

A timeline of the Gospels · dates are approximate and scholars vary

How to use this timeline

This timeline follows Jesus from the angel’s announcement to Mary to his ascension from the Mount of Olives. It numbers all 35 miracles Jesus performs in the Gospels, letters the 10 signs from heaven that surround his life, shows 38 Old Testament prophecies at the moment they were fulfilled, and places 30 key events between them so you can see how they fit together.

The Gospels do not give calendar dates. Jesus was born about 6–4 BC (some date it 3–2 BC) and began his ministry at about age thirty. John mentions at least three Passovers, so the ministry lasted about two and a half to three and a half years; the two most common datings are about AD 27–30 and AD 29–33. The order follows a standard harmony of the Gospels, and harmonies differ on some details. The Gospels also say Jesus did many more signs than are written (John 20:30; 21:25); these are the ones described individually.

Only one miracle, the feeding of the five thousand (19), is in all four Gospels. Found only in Matthew: 17, 18, 26; only in Mark: 22, 24; only in Luke: 3, 11, 28, 29, 31, 34; only in John: 1, 2, 8, 27, 30, 35.

Prophecies fulfilled

These 38 Old Testament passages are the ones the New Testament itself says Jesus fulfilled, or that Jesus applied to himself. Each appears in the timeline as a shaded box at the moment it was fulfilled, with the Old Testament words quoted from the ASV. Christians have long seen many more (Luke 24:27, 44), but this list keeps to the ones Scripture names.

Map: where the miracles happened

Miracles 6, 9 and 12 happened in unnamed towns of Galilee, and 28 and 29 on the final journey toward Jerusalem, so they are not placed on the map.

Map: where the prophecies were fulfilled

Most of the prophecies came true in and around Jerusalem in Jesus’ last week; the plan on the next page shows those sites. Hosea’s “out of Egypt” (Matthew 2:15) was fulfilled beyond the map to the southwest.

Plan: Jerusalem in Jesus’ last week

The sites of the last supper, the trials, the crucifixion and the tomb are known only by tradition, and some have alternatives (marked). The prophecies of P-numbers not shown here (such as Nicodemus and the voice from heaven) were fulfilled in the city at places the Gospels do not name.

phases.title: Birth and Early Years
phases.when: When: About 6–4 BC to about AD 8 · Where: Nazareth, Bethlehem, Egypt, Jerusalem
phases.intro: Matthew and Luke tell of Jesus' birth from different angles: Matthew follows Joseph and the wise men, Luke follows Mary and the shepherds. Heaven announces the birth again and again.

entries.title: The annunciation and the virgin conception
entries.text: The angel Gabriel told Mary she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear the Son of the Most High. An angel told Joseph in a dream to take Mary as his wife and to name the child Jesus.

prophecies.quote: “Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.”

“When thy days are fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, that shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.”
prophecies.to: Luke 1:32–33 (the throne of his father David)

entries.title: Jesus is born in Bethlehem
entries.text: Joseph and Mary traveled to Bethlehem for the census, and Jesus was born there and laid in a manger, in the days of Herod the king.

prophecies.quote: “But thou, Beth-lehem Ephrathah, which art little to be among the thousands of Judah, out of thee shall one come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth are from of old, from everlasting.”

entries.title: Angels appear to the shepherds
entries.text: An angel announced the birth of a Savior, Christ the Lord, and a multitude of the heavenly host praised God. The shepherds found the child as they had been told.

entries.title: Presented in the temple; Simeon and Anna
entries.text: When the days of purification were fulfilled (about forty days), Jesus was presented in the temple. Simeon, told by the Spirit he would see the Lord's Christ, took him in his arms; the prophetess Anna spoke of him to all who waited for redemption.

entries.title: The star and the wise men
entries.text: Wise men from the east followed a star to Jerusalem and then to the house in Bethlehem, worshiped the child and gave gold, frankincense and myrrh. Warned in a dream, they went home another way.

entries.title: Warnings in dreams: Egypt and Nazareth
entries.text: An angel warned Joseph in a dream to flee to Egypt before Herod killed the boys of Bethlehem, and later told him to return. A further warning sent the family to Nazareth in Galilee.

prophecies.quote: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.”
“Thus saith Jehovah: A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children; she refuseth to be comforted for her children, because they are not.”

entries.title: At twelve in the temple
entries.text: After Passover the boy Jesus stayed behind in the temple, listening to the teachers and asking them questions. He told his parents he must be in his Father's house.

phases.title: Preparation
phases.when: When: About age 30 (Luke 3:23) · Where: The Jordan River and the Judean wilderness
phases.intro: After about eighteen silent years in Nazareth, Jesus came to John at the Jordan. The Father's voice and the Spirit mark the start of his public work.

entries.title: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness
entries.meta: The Jordan River · Matthew 3:1–12; Mark 1:1–8; Luke 3:1–18; John 1:19–28
entries.text: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius, John called Israel to repent and be baptized, and promised one mightier than himself.

prophecies.quote: “The voice of one that crieth, Prepare ye in the wilderness the way of Jehovah; make level in the desert a highway for our God. Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low; and the uneven shall be made level, and the rough places a plain: and the glory of Jehovah shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken it.”

“Behold, I send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom ye desire, behold, he cometh, saith Jehovah of hosts.”

entries.title: The baptism: the Spirit and the Father's voice
entries.meta: The Jordan River · Matthew 3:13–17; Mark 1:9–11; Luke 3:21–22; John 1:29–34
entries.text: As Jesus came up from the water, the heavens opened, the Holy Spirit descended like a dove, and a voice from heaven declared him the beloved Son.

entries.title: Forty days of temptation
entries.meta: The wilderness of Judea · Matthew 4:1–11; Mark 1:12–13; Luke 4:1–13
entries.text: Led by the Spirit, Jesus fasted forty days and answered each temptation of the devil with Scripture. Angels then ministered to him.

entries.title: The first disciples
entries.meta: Bethany beyond the Jordan; Galilee · John 1:35–51
entries.text: Andrew and another disciple of John followed Jesus; Andrew brought Peter, and Philip brought Nathanael, whom Jesus had seen under the fig tree before they met.

phases.title: The Early Ministry
phases.when: When: Around the first Passover (John 2:13), about the first year · Where: Cana, Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria
phases.intro: John's Gospel alone records this first year, before Jesus settled in Capernaum. John counts his miracles as signs that reveal who he is.

entries.title: Water turned into wine
entries.text: At a wedding where the wine ran out, Jesus had six stone water jars filled with water, and it became good wine. John calls this the beginning of his signs, and his disciples believed in him.

entries.title: The first Passover: Jesus clears the temple
entries.text: Jesus drove the sellers and money-changers out of the temple and spoke of the temple of his body, which would be raised in three days.

prophecies.quote: “For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up; And the reproaches of them that reproach thee are fallen upon me.”

entries.title: Nicodemus comes by night
entries.text: Jesus told the Pharisee Nicodemus that a man must be born anew, and that God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son.

prophecies.quote: “And Moses made a serpent of brass, and set it upon the standard: and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked unto the serpent of brass, he lived.”

entries.title: The Samaritan woman at Jacob's well
entries.text: Jesus offered living water to a Samaritan woman, told her about her past, and declared himself the Messiah. Many in her town believed.

entries.title: The official's son healed from a distance
entries.meta: Cana; the son at Capernaum · John 4:46–54
entries.text: A royal official begged Jesus to come before his son died. Jesus told him to go, his son lived; the fever left the boy at that very hour, about sixteen miles away. John calls it the second sign.

phases.title: The Great Galilean Ministry
phases.when: When: About the second year, centered on Capernaum · Where: Capernaum and the towns of Galilee
phases.intro: Jesus made Capernaum his base. Crowds came from every region, and the Gospels crowd these months with healings, teaching and the calling of the Twelve.

entries.title: Rejected in the synagogue at Nazareth
entries.text: Jesus read from Isaiah 61 and said it was fulfilled that day. His hometown turned against him and tried to throw him from a cliff, but he passed through them.

prophecies.quote: “The Spirit of the Lord Jehovah is upon me; because Jehovah hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; to proclaim the year of Jehovah’s favor, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn;”

entries.title: Jesus moves to Capernaum and calls fishermen
entries.text: Jesus began preaching that the kingdom of heaven was at hand, and called Peter, Andrew, James and John to become fishers of men.

prophecies.quote: “But there shall be no gloom to her that was in anguish. In the former time he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time hath he made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations. The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwelt in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.”

entries.title: The great catch of fish
entries.text: After a night of catching nothing, Peter let down the nets at Jesus' word and caught so many fish the nets began to break. Peter fell at his knees, and the fishermen left everything to follow him.

entries.title: An unclean spirit driven out in the synagogue
entries.text: A man with an unclean spirit cried out in the synagogue. Jesus rebuked the spirit and it came out, and the people were amazed at his authority.

entries.title: Peter's mother-in-law healed
entries.text: Jesus took her by the hand and the fever left her, and she served them. That evening the whole city gathered at the door, and he healed many and cast out demons.

prophecies.quote: “Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows; yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.”

entries.title: A leper cleansed
entries.meta: A town in Galilee · Matthew 8:1–4; Mark 1:40–45; Luke 5:12–16
entries.text: A leper knelt and said, “If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.” Jesus touched him, the one person no one would touch, and he was cleansed at once.

entries.title: A paralyzed man lowered through the roof
entries.text: Four friends dug through the roof to lower him to Jesus. Jesus forgave his sins and then told him to take up his bed and walk, to show he had authority to forgive.

entries.title: Matthew the tax collector is called
entries.text: Jesus called Matthew from his tax booth and ate with tax collectors and sinners, saying he came to call sinners.

entries.title: The invalid at the Pool of Bethesda
entries.text: A man who had been ill thirty-eight years was told to rise, take up his bed and walk, and he did. It was the Sabbath, and the leaders began to seek to kill Jesus for calling God his Father.

entries.title: The man with a withered hand
entries.meta: A synagogue in Galilee · Matthew 12:9–14; Mark 3:1–6; Luke 6:6–11
entries.text: On the Sabbath Jesus told the man to stretch out his hand, and it was restored. The Pharisees went out and plotted with the Herodians how to destroy him.

prophecies.quote: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delighteth: I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the Gentiles. He will not cry, nor lift up his voice, nor cause it to be heard in the street. A bruised reed will he not break, and a dimly burning wick will he not quench: he will bring forth justice in truth. He will not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set justice in the earth; and the isles shall wait for his law.”

entries.title: The Twelve chosen; the Sermon on the Mount
entries.meta: A mountain in Galilee · Matthew 5–7; Mark 3:13–19; Luke 6:12–49
entries.text: After a night in prayer Jesus chose twelve apostles, then taught the Beatitudes, the Lord's Prayer and the wise and foolish builders.

entries.title: The centurion's servant
entries.text: A Roman centurion asked Jesus only to say the word, since he too was a man under authority. Jesus marveled at his faith, and the servant was healed that hour.

entries.title: The widow's son raised at Nain
entries.text: Jesus met a funeral procession for a widow's only son. He had compassion on her, touched the bier and told the young man to arise, and he sat up and began to speak.

prophecies.quote: “Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. Then shall the lame man leap as a hart, and the tongue of the dumb shall sing; for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.”
prophecies.to: Luke 7:18–23; Matthew 11:2–6 (Jesus' answer to John the Baptist)

entries.title: A blind and mute man freed from a demon
entries.text: When Jesus healed him, the crowds wondered if he was the Son of David, but the Pharisees said he cast out demons by Beelzebub. Jesus answered that a house divided cannot stand.

entries.title: Parables by the sea
entries.meta: The Sea of Galilee · Matthew 13:1–52; Mark 4:1–34; Luke 8:4–18
entries.text: From a boat Jesus taught the sower, the mustard seed, the hidden treasure and other parables of the kingdom.

prophecies.quote: “And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.”
“I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter dark sayings of old,”

entries.title: The storm calmed
entries.meta: The Sea of Galilee · Matthew 8:23–27; Mark 4:35–41; Luke 8:22–25
entries.text: A great storm swamped the boat while Jesus slept. He rebuked the wind and the sea and there was a great calm, and the disciples asked what manner of man this was.

entries.title: The demoniac called Legion
entries.meta: The country of the Gerasenes, east shore · Matthew 8:28–34; Mark 5:1–20; Luke 8:26–39
entries.text: A man no chains could hold lived among the tombs; Matthew mentions two men. Jesus sent the demons into a herd of swine, and the healed man went through the Decapolis telling what Jesus had done.

entries.title: The woman with the issue of blood
entries.text: After twelve years of bleeding and spending all she had on physicians, she touched the border of his garment in the crowd and was healed. Jesus told her that her faith had made her whole.

entries.title: Jairus' daughter raised
entries.text: The synagogue ruler's twelve-year-old daughter died while Jesus was on his way. Jesus took her by the hand and said, “Talitha cumi,” and she rose up and walked.

entries.title: Two blind men
entries.text: Two blind men followed him crying for mercy. Jesus asked if they believed he could do this, touched their eyes, and their eyes were opened.

entries.title: A mute man freed from a demon
entries.text: When the demon was cast out the mute man spoke, and the crowds said nothing like it had ever been seen in Israel.

entries.title: A second rejection at Nazareth
entries.text: His hometown was offended at the carpenter's son, and he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

entries.title: The Twelve sent out; John the Baptist killed
entries.text: Jesus gave the Twelve authority over demons and diseases and sent them out two by two. Meanwhile Herod Antipas beheaded John the Baptist.

phases.title: Around the Second Passover: Later Galilee
phases.when: When: From the second Passover (John 6:4) to the autumn · Where: Around the Sea of Galilee; Tyre and Sidon; the Decapolis; Caesarea Philippi
phases.intro: The feeding of the five thousand is the one miracle in all four Gospels. Afterward Jesus often withdrew from the crowds with the Twelve, and began to speak openly of his death.

entries.title: Five thousand fed
entries.meta: Near Bethsaida · Matthew 14:13–21; Mark 6:30–44; Luke 9:10–17; John 6:1–14
entries.text: With five loaves and two fishes Jesus fed about five thousand men besides women and children, and twelve baskets of pieces were left over. The Passover was near.

entries.title: Jesus walks on the water
entries.meta: The Sea of Galilee · Matthew 14:22–33; Mark 6:45–52; John 6:16–21
entries.text: In the night Jesus came to the disciples walking on the sea. Peter walked toward him, began to sink when he saw the wind, and Jesus caught him. Those in the boat worshiped him.

entries.title: Healings at Gennesaret; the bread of life
entries.text: As many as touched the border of his garment were made whole. In Capernaum Jesus called himself the bread of life, and many disciples turned back.

entries.title: The Syrophoenician woman's daughter
entries.meta: The region of Tyre and Sidon · Matthew 15:21–28; Mark 7:24–30
entries.text: A Gentile mother answered that even the dogs eat the crumbs from the master's table. Jesus praised her great faith, and her daughter was healed from that hour.

entries.title: A deaf man with a speech impediment
entries.text: Jesus took him aside, put his fingers in his ears, touched his tongue and said, “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened.” He heard and spoke plainly.

entries.title: Four thousand fed
entries.meta: The Decapolis, by the Sea of Galilee · Matthew 15:32–39; Mark 8:1–10
entries.text: After three days with Jesus in a largely Gentile region, a crowd of four thousand men besides women and children was fed with seven loaves and a few small fishes, with seven baskets left.

entries.title: The blind man at Bethsaida
entries.text: The only healing done in two stages: at first the man saw men like walking trees, then Jesus touched his eyes again and he saw everything clearly.

entries.title: Peter's confession; Jesus foretells his death
entries.text: Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ. From then on Jesus taught that he must suffer, be killed and be raised the third day.

entries.title: The transfiguration
entries.meta: A high mountain (traditionally Tabor, possibly Hermon) · Matthew 17:1–8; Mark 9:2–8; Luke 9:28–36
entries.text: Before Peter, James and John, Jesus' face shone like the sun, Moses and Elijah talked with him, and a voice from a bright cloud said to hear him. Peter recalls it in 2 Peter 1:16–18.

entries.title: The boy with an unclean spirit
entries.meta: Below the mountain · Matthew 17:14–20; Mark 9:14–29; Luke 9:37–43
entries.text: The disciples could not help a boy thrown into fire and water by a spirit. His father cried, “I believe; help thou mine unbelief,” and Jesus cast the spirit out.

entries.title: The coin in the fish's mouth
entries.text: Asked about the temple tax, Jesus sent Peter to catch a fish, and in its mouth was a shekel to pay for them both.

phases.title: The Later Judean and Perean Ministry
phases.when: When: About the final six months, from Tabernacles to the last Passover · Where: Jerusalem, Judea, Perea beyond the Jordan, Jericho, Bethany
phases.intro: Jesus set his face to go to Jerusalem (Luke 9:51). John follows him at the feasts in Jerusalem; Luke follows the long journey through Samaria, Judea and Perea.

entries.title: The Feast of Tabernacles; the seventy sent out
entries.text: At the feast Jesus invited the thirsty to come to him and said he was the light of the world. He sent seventy others ahead of him in pairs.

entries.title: The man born blind
entries.meta: Jerusalem, the pool of Siloam · John 9:1–41
entries.text: Jesus made clay, anointed the man's eyes and sent him to wash in Siloam, and he came back seeing. Questioned by the Pharisees, he said, “One thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.”

entries.title: The Feast of Dedication
entries.text: In winter Jesus said, “I and the Father are one.” They tried to stone him, and he withdrew beyond the Jordan.

entries.title: A woman bent over for eighteen years
entries.meta: A synagogue on the way to Jerusalem · Luke 13:10–17
entries.text: Jesus laid his hands on her on the Sabbath and she was made straight and glorified God. He called her a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound.

entries.title: A man with dropsy
entries.text: At a Sabbath meal Jesus healed a man swollen with fluid and asked who would not pull out an ox fallen into a well on the Sabbath.

entries.title: Lazarus raised from the dead
entries.text: Lazarus had been in the tomb four days. Jesus wept, told Martha he is the resurrection and the life, and called, “Lazarus, come forth.” This sign moved the council to plot his death (John 11:45–53).

entries.title: Ten lepers cleansed
entries.text: Ten lepers were cleansed as they went to show themselves to the priests. Only one, a Samaritan, came back to give thanks.

entries.title: Children blessed; the rich young ruler
entries.text: Jesus welcomed little children and told a rich man to sell all and follow him.

entries.title: Blind Bartimaeus
entries.text: A blind beggar kept crying, “Thou son of David, have mercy on me.” Jesus called him and restored his sight, and he followed Jesus on the road. Matthew mentions two blind men.

entries.title: Zacchaeus; Mary anoints Jesus at Bethany
entries.meta: Jericho; Bethany · Luke 19:1–10; John 12:1–8; Matthew 26:6–13; Mark 14:3–9
entries.text: A chief tax collector received Jesus gladly and repented. Six days before the Passover, Mary anointed Jesus' feet with costly ointment.

phases.title: The Passion Week
phases.when: When: The final Passover, AD 30 or 33 · Where: Jerusalem, Bethany, the Mount of Olives
phases.intro: All four Gospels slow down for this one week, which fills about a third of their pages.

entries.title: The triumphal entry
entries.text: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey while crowds spread garments and branches and cried Hosanna. He wept over the city.

prophecies.quote: “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy king cometh unto thee; he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, even upon a colt the foal of an ass.”
“Blessed be he that cometh in the name of Jehovah: We have blessed you out of the house of Jehovah.”

entries.title: The fig tree withers
entries.meta: On the road from Bethany · Matthew 21:18–22; Mark 11:12–14, 20–25
entries.text: Finding a fig tree with leaves but no fruit, Jesus said no one would eat from it again; by the next morning it had withered from the roots, and he taught the disciples about faith and prayer.

entries.title: The temple cleansed; the blind and lame healed there
entries.meta: The temple, Jerusalem · Matthew 21:12–17; Mark 11:15–19; Luke 19:45–48
entries.text: Jesus drove out the buyers and sellers, calling the temple a house of prayer. The blind and the lame came to him there and he healed them.

prophecies.quote: “even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt-offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”
“Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou established strength, Because of thine adversaries, That thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger.”
“The stone which the builders rejected Is become the head of the corner. This is Jehovah’s doing; It is marvellous in our eyes.”
prophecies.to: Matthew 21:42; Mark 12:10–11; Luke 20:17; Acts 4:11 (Jesus applies it to himself that week)

entries.title: A voice from heaven
entries.text: When Jesus prayed, “Father, glorify thy name,” a voice came from heaven: “I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.” Some said it thundered.

prophecies.quote: “Who hath believed our message? and to whom hath the arm of Jehovah been revealed?”

“Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.”

entries.title: The Last Supper
entries.meta: An upper room in Jerusalem · Matthew 26:17–30; Mark 14:12–26; Luke 22:7–38; John 13–17
entries.text: Jesus washed the disciples' feet, gave them the bread and the cup of the new covenant, foretold Judas' betrayal and Peter's denial, and prayed for them.

prophecies.quote: “Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, Who did eat of my bread, Hath lifted up his heel against me.”

“Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Jehovah of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered; and I will turn my hand upon the little ones.”

“Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he poured out his soul unto death, and was numbered with the transgressors: yet he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.”
“They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head: They that would cut me off, being mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty: That which I took not away I have to restore.”

entries.title: The servant's ear healed
entries.meta: Gethsemane, on the Mount of Olives · Luke 22:47–53 (compare John 18:10–11)
entries.text: When Peter cut off the ear of the high priest's servant, whom John names Malchus, Jesus touched his ear and healed him: the last healing before the cross.

entries.title: The trials
entries.text: Jesus was questioned by Annas and Caiaphas, condemned by the council, sent by Pilate to Herod Antipas and back, and handed over to be crucified.

prophecies.quote: “And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my hire; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my hire thirty pieces of silver. And Jehovah said unto me, Cast it unto the potter, the goodly price that I was prized at by them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them unto the potter, in the house of Jehovah.”

“He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he opened not his mouth; as a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before its shearers is dumb, so he opened not his mouth. By oppression and judgment he was taken away; and as for his generation, who among them considered that he was cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of my people to whom the stroke was due?”

entries.title: The crucifixion
entries.meta: Golgotha, outside Jerusalem · Matthew 27:27–56; Mark 15:16–41; Luke 23:26–49; John 19:16–37
entries.text: Jesus was crucified between two robbers. Soldiers divided his garments, he cried out to his Father and was given vinegar to drink, and when he had died a soldier pierced his side instead of breaking his legs.

prophecies.quote: “They part my garments among them, And upon my vesture do they cast lots.”
“My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning?”
prophecies.to: Matthew 27:46; Mark 15:34 (Jesus' words on the cross)

prophecies.quote: “They gave me also gall for my food; And in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.”
“In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth aught of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.”

“And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplication; and they shall look unto me whom they have pierced; and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his first-born.”

entries.title: Signs at the crucifixion
entries.meta: Golgotha, outside Jerusalem · Matthew 27:45–56; Mark 15:33–41; Luke 23:44–49
entries.text: Darkness covered the land from the sixth hour to the ninth, the veil of the temple was torn in two, the earth shook and rocks split, and tombs were opened. The centurion confessed him the Son of God.

entries.title: The burial
entries.meta: Joseph of Arimathea's tomb · Matthew 27:57–66; Mark 15:42–47; Luke 23:50–56; John 19:38–42
entries.text: Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus laid Jesus' body in a new tomb, and the tomb was sealed and guarded.

phases.title: Resurrection to Ascension
phases.when: When: Forty days (Acts 1:3) · Where: Jerusalem, Emmaus, Galilee, the Mount of Olives
phases.intro: The resurrection is the sign behind every other sign. Over forty days the risen Jesus appeared to individuals, to groups and once to more than five hundred people.

entries.title: The resurrection
entries.meta: The garden tomb, Jerusalem · Matthew 28:1–8; Mark 16:1–8; Luke 24:1–12; John 20:1–10
entries.text: Early on the first day of the week there was a great earthquake, an angel rolled away the stone, and the women found the tomb empty. The angel said, “He is not here; for he is risen.”

prophecies.quote: “For thou wilt not leave my soul to Sheol; Neither wilt thou suffer thy holy one to see corruption.”
“I will tell of the decree: Jehovah said unto me, Thou art my son; This day have I begotten thee.”

entries.title: Appearances in Jerusalem and Emmaus
entries.meta: Jerusalem; the road to Emmaus · Matthew 28:9–10; Mark 16:9–14; Luke 24:13–49; John 20:11–29; 1 Corinthians 15:5
entries.text: Jesus appeared to Mary Magdalene, to the other women, to two disciples on the road to Emmaus, to Peter, and to the disciples, first without Thomas and then with him. (Mark 16:9–20 is missing from some of the oldest manuscripts.)

entries.title: The second great catch of fish
entries.text: After another night of catching nothing, the disciples cast the net on the right side at the word of a stranger on the shore and caught 153 large fish. the disciple whom Jesus loved said, “It is the Lord.” Jesus then restored Peter (John 21:15–19).

entries.title: Appearances in Galilee and to many
entries.meta: A mountain in Galilee · Matthew 28:16–20; Mark 16:15–18; 1 Corinthians 15:6–7
entries.text: Jesus appeared to more than five hundred at once and to James, and on a mountain in Galilee he sent the eleven to make disciples of all the nations, promising to be with them always.

entries.title: The ascension
entries.meta: The Mount of Olives, near Bethany · Luke 24:50–53; Acts 1:6–11; Mark 16:19
entries.text: Jesus blessed the disciples and was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight. Two men in white said he would come again in the same way.

prophecies.quote: “Jehovah saith unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, Until I make thine enemies thy footstool.”

“Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led away captives; Thou hast received gifts among men, Yea, among the rebellious also, that Jehovah God might dwell with them.” “Many other signs therefore did Jesus in the presence of the disciples, which are not written in this book: but these are written, that ye may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye may have life in his name.”
